summary: Defines a YANG module for managing logical network elements, meaning logical partitions of a device such as logical systems or logical routers. It is compatible with the Network Management Datastore Architecture from RFC 8342. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: A single big computer can pretend to be several smaller ones. This document describes the settings list for creating and managing those pretend devices inside one real box.

questions: what is a logical network element
subtitle: A YANG module for carving one network device into independently managed logical devices, such as logical routers.

tldr.problem: Many network devices can be partitioned into logical systems or logical routers, each managed on its own, but there was no standard NMDA-compliant YANG model for creating them and assigning resources to them.
tldr.mechanism: The ietf-logical-network-element module defines a list of logical network elements (LNEs), each with a schema mount point for its own data, plus a leaf that binds an interface to an LNE.
tldr.outcome: An operator can create and delete LNEs with ordinary list operations and assign interfaces to them. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and is not obsoleted.

today: RFC 8530 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is the definition of the ietf-logical-network-element module.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 8530 defines a YANG module (RFC 6020) that follows the Network Management Datastore Architecture (RFC 8342). It supports creating logical network elements (LNEs) on a network device. An LNE is an independently managed virtual device made up of resources allocated to it from the host or parent device.

The RFC compares this to a virtual machine running on a host system: the LNE is the "Guest" and the containing device is the "Host". LNEs may be built with host-virtualization technology, but that is not required. Vendors use terms such as logical system, logical router, and virtual switch, chassis, or fabric.

Each LNE has its own YANG-modeled data, independent of the host and other LNEs. Several LNEs can each have a Tunnel0 interface without conflict. An LNE may have its own management servers, possibly including independent NETCONF or RESTCONF instances.
sections.eli5: Think of an apartment building: each apartment has its own rules, furniture and mailbox, even though it is all one building.

sections.title: Overview and the Interface Augmentation
sections.content:
The RFC considers devices that support Routing Area protocols and functions, such as routers, firewalls and hosts, whether physical or virtual. A device may subdivide its resources into LNEs. Each LNE may also support VRF and Virtual Switching Instance functions, called Network Instances (NIs), whose model is in RFC 8529.

Interfaces are the one host resource this document handles, because the interface management model (RFC 8343) is the only module that currently defines host resources. The module augments it with a single leaf, bind-lne-name, which names the LNE an interface belongs to. Future modules that control host resources are expected to provide parallel support where appropriate.

To place an interface in both an LNE and a Network Instance, it is first assigned to the LNE, and then the LNE's own representation of the interface is assigned to the NI.
sections.eli5: Each plug on the back of the box has a label saying which pretend device owns it. Only the label is added; the plugs themselves are described elsewhere.

sections.title: The LNE Data Model
sections.content:
The module has a top-level logical-network-elements container holding a list logical-network-element keyed by name. Each entry has:

  • name, a device-wide unique identifier;
  • managed, a boolean saying whether the host can reach the LNE's data through the root mount point (default true);
  • description, free text;
  • root, a schema mount point (RFC 8528) under which the LNE's own models appear.

An LNE root MUST contain at least the YANG library (RFC 7895) and the interface module. Beyond those, any module that may be present on a top-level network device MAY also be present for the LNE, and the list of modules depends on the implementation. The module also defines a bind-lne-name-failed notification.
sections.eli5: The list is a roster of the pretend devices. Each has a name, a note saying if the landlord may peek inside, a description, and a door into its own rooms.

sections.title: Creating LNEs and Assigning Interfaces
sections.content:
Clients control LNEs with existing list operations. Creating a list entry instantiates a new LNE, and deleting an entry destroys it. The models mounted under an LNE root depend on the server implementation.

Once an LNE exists, setting bind-lne-name on an interface to a valid LNE name means the implementation MUST take whatever steps are needed to assign the interface, or give an error explaining why it failed. The failure may come while processing the set, or later after asynchronous processing. In the latter case the bind-lne-name-failed notification, which carries the interface name, the LNE name and optional error information, reports it.

On success the implementation MUST also give the LNE a system-created interface. Its name is a local matter: on the host it might be Ethernet0/1 while inside the LNE it is eth1. It SHOULD appear in the LNE's own instance of the interface model.
sections.eli5: You make a new pretend device by adding a line to the roster, then stick its label on a plug. If the plug cannot be handed over, you get a message saying why.

sections.title: Managing an LNE
sections.content:
There are two views. From inside the LNE, management goes through the LNE's own interfaces such as NETCONF and SNMP, with the LNE root presented as the device root. Only LNE-associated resources show up, so from a management view an LNE looks like a physical network device. Initial configuration is a local implementation matter.

From the host, access depends on the managed leaf. When it is false, the LNE can only be managed from inside, and any attempt to access data below its root MUST fail with error-tag access-denied and error-app-tag lne-not-managed. This value may be fixed to false, for example when the LNE is a virtual machine under a traditional hypervisor. When true, LNE information SHALL be accessible from the host, and also modifiable if the schema mount config leaf is true.

An implementation MAY describe an LNE's schema with either the inline or the shared-schema approach of RFC 8528. Inline is expected where managed is always false; shared-schema suits LNEs that all use the same schema.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the landlord can look into an apartment and sometimes the door is locked. A flag on each apartment says which, and locked apartments answer "access denied".

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The data is accessed through protocols such as NETCONF (RFC 6241) or RESTCONF (RFC 8040), and access can be restricted with NACM (RFC 8341). The RFC says LNE information is fundamentally no different from other interface or device configuration already covered elsewhere.

It lists three sensitive writable nodes: the LNE list itself, the managed leaf, and the bind-lne-name leaf. The managed leaf deserves extra care where a different party manages the LNE and does not want to share its data with the host operator. Removing an interface from an LNE is like physically removing it from the device, so implementations can reject reassignments. Unauthorized access can cause network malfunctions and delivery of packets to inappropriate destinations.
sections.eli5: Whoever can edit the roster or move the plug labels can break the whole building, so only trusted people should be allowed to.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The document registers the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-logical-network-element in the IETF XML Registry (RFC 3688) and registers the YANG module ietf-logical-network-element with prefix lne in the YANG Module Names registry.
sections.eli5: The module gets its official name and nickname in the public registry so nobody else uses them.
